utterance: Good morning, Mark. What can I do for you today?
reply: Morning. I have had a cough and a fever for three days now, and I am feeling pretty rotten because it is just not shifting. It started as a dry, hacking cough and I have been burning up on and off, roasting even without a thermometer. Since yesterday I am bringing stuff up that is a rusty, brownish colour, though it was clear at first, and there is a sharp pain low down on the right side round towards my back that catches me when I take a deep breath or cough.

awards.label: Chest pain with breathing or coughing

finding: Bronchial breathing with coarse crackles at the right base. Left base clear.
Dull to percussion at the right base. Left base resonant.

utterance: Can you tell me more about the pain on the right side? Is it related to anything else, like movement or position?
reply: It just catches me when I take a deep breath or cough, starting yesterday, and I am not sure if it has anything to do with movement or position. I really need to get this sorted out before the year 12 exams next week.

result: Right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms. Other lobes clear. No pleural effusion. Normal heart size.

utterance: I'm going to order a chest X-ray for you. In the meantime, I want to check if you have any other symptoms like shortness of breath or sweats.
reply: I only noticed that going up the stairs and on the way in from the car park, but sitting here I am alright. I have not noticed anything like sweats. An X-ray sounds like a bit of a hassle, but if we have to do it, we have to do it.

utterance: The X-ray shows consolidation in the right lower lobe, which is consistent with pneumonia. I'm going to prescribe you some antibiotics to help clear the infection. Have you had any recent travel or exposure to anyone with a similar illness?
reply: No, I have not been anywhere, just school and home. Pneumonia sounds serious, and the exams start next week, so I just want to know how long before I am back on my feet.

utterance: I'm prescribing amoxycillin for you. You should start feeling better within a few days, but it's crucial to complete the full course. If your symptoms worsen or you experience any difficulty breathing, chest pain, or high fever, please seek immediate medical attention.
reply: Right, I will take the tablets properly and try to get some rest, but I really need to be back in front of the class by Monday if at all possible.

awards.label: Unsafe: Penicillin in a penicillin-allergic patient
